text:
olivia: Heads-up — canary promo for 2026.03.21 stalled during deploybot prefetch. Deploybot shows checksum mismatch on artifact manifest vs cache. Promotion paused.

deploy-bot: [status] prefetch failed for service=ingest, shard=2, reason=manifest-checksum-mismatch, artifact=img:sha256:abcd...ef01. Auto-fallback attempted -> no compatible blob found.

raj: Ugh. This looks like the registry pushed a new layer but our prefetch cache has the old manifest stamp. Could be S3 replication lag or a concurrent reupload.

nic: Logs — from the runner: ```ERROR Prefetcher: manifest checksum 0x9f7a != expected 0x3b2c (object: s3://redwood-artifacts/ingest/20260321/manifest.json)```

olivia: Any quick unblock? Can we force ignore checksum and promote, or do we need to rollback? Need decision for release window.

raj: Don't force-promo. If the manifest points to missing blobs we'll break canary traffic. Options: 1) pin to last-good digest and promote that, 2) flush the prefetch cache + re-run prefetch, 3) roll back canary to previous image.

nic: I can trigger a targeted cache flush for the shard that's failing and then re-run prefetch. That should fix if it's replication/lazy-ttl. ETA ~10m if no other issues.

tao: If we go with pin, we should update the release notes and internal changelog to indicate a manual pin and retry later. Who owns the release note entry? I can do it once we decide.

olivia: @nic do the flush+prefetch attempt. If prefetch still fails after one retry, we'll pin to the last-good digest and promote. Can @raj / @tao approve that flow?

raj: +1 to that plan. Keep traffic off the canary until promote completes.

tao: +1. I'll prep a note: "Canary temporarily pinned to previous digest due to artifact prefetch checksum mismatch; follow-up investigation on registry replication."

deploy-bot: [command echo] `deploybot prefetch --service=ingest --shard=2 --force` requested by nic. Run id: rb-20260321-17.

nic: Running flush + prefetch now. Will post result.

sre-bot: [alert] Canary_sla_drop: ingest-canary latency spiked 15% since promo attempt at 1768509988. Notified on-call.

nic: Prefetch attempt completed — still failing with same checksum mismatch. I rechecked S3 object timestamps; manifest has been re-uploaded within the last minute which created a transient digest drift.

olivia: Ok, we've hit transient registry consistency. Proceed with pin and manual promote. Nic — do pin and then run promote to canary-only. After that, schedule a follow-up to re-run a clean promote once registry consistency confirms.

nic: Pinned image to last-good digest `img:sha256:9012...bcd3`. Running `deploybot promote --service=ingest --image=sha256:9012...bcd3 --to=canary --reason="prefetch checksum mismatch"` now.

deploy-bot: [action] Promotion initiated by nic -> target=canary, image=sha256:9012...bcd3, id=prom-20260321-9. Will run health checks.

sre-bot: [monitor] Healthcheck: ingest-canary passed readiness probes. Traffic shift to canary at 10% completed.

olivia: Great. Tao, please add the release note and mark change-window as "partial: canary pinned; full promo deferred". We'll reconvene in 30m to decide on re-promote.

tao: Added note in release doc and created a GH issue to track follow-up: "registry replication caused prefetch checksum drift — verify upload path and add idempotent manifest writes."

raj: Postmortem candidate if we see recurrence. Also let's add a shortterm check in the prefetcher to compare manifest write timestamps and retry read-after-write for 30s before failing.

olivia: Agreed. For now we keep the canary pinned and continue with release window as scoped. Closing this thread after follow-up confirmation unless anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

nic: I'll file a small PR for the prefetcher retry logic and link it to the follow-up issue.

deploy-bot: [log] prom-20260321-9 completed, canary at digest sha256:9012...bcd3, rollback-safe=true.

sre-bot: [info] Incident: ingest-canary temporary stall resolved (duration ~6m)"
